```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(pdmS7)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 3.6, dpi = 110
)
pal <- c("#236b83", "#a26421", "#5b8c3a", "#8a3b6b", "#444444", "#b23b3b", "#9aa7b0")
```

This guide takes you from your own data files to a running, scored, saved model in about
ten steps. It assumes you know some R, but nothing about pdmS7. For what the model does
inside, read [How the PDM works](pdm-explained.html) alongside.

# 1. What you need

Two files, one row per time step:

| File | Columns | Units |
|---|---|---|
| Forcing | `time`, `rain`, `pet` | Rain and potential evaporation as **totals per time step**, in mm |
| Flow | `time`, `q_m3s` | Measured river flow in m3/s; leave gaps empty |

Times should be in UTC, written like `2024-01-31T09:00:00Z` or `2024-01-31 09:00`, at a fixed
step: 15 minutes, an hour, a day. You also need the catchment area in km2.

So that this guide runs anywhere, the next step makes example files. With your own data,
skip it and point the paths at your files.

```{r make-files}
folder <- file.path(tempdir(), "my-catchment")
dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
set.seed(21)
n <- 24 * 90
time <- seq(as.POSIXct("2024-01-01", tz = "UTC"), by = 3600, length.out = n)
rain <- ifelse(stats::runif(n) < 0.07, stats::rgamma(n, 0.7, scale = 3.5), 0)
truth <- pdm_presets("standard")
truth$area_km2 <- 64
truth$recharge$kg <- 250
truth$fc <- 1.1
truth$surface$k1 <- 3
truth$surface$k2 <- 8
flow <- run_pdm(pdm_from_config(truth), data.frame(rain = rain, pet = 0.06),
                initial_state_from_flow(pdm_from_config(truth), 0.8, 0.7))$output$q_m3s
flow <- round(flow * exp(stats::rnorm(n, 0, 0.04)), 3)
flow[24 * 40 + 1:30] <- NA
stamp <- format(time, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
data.table::fwrite(data.frame(time = stamp, rain = round(rain, 2), pet = 0.06),
                   file.path(folder, "forcing.csv"))
data.table::fwrite(data.frame(time = stamp, q_m3s = flow), file.path(folder, "flow.csv"))
```

# 2. Read and check the data

```{r read}
forcing <- data.table::fread(file.path(folder, "forcing.csv"))
observed <- data.table::fread(file.path(folder, "flow.csv"))
forcing$time <- as.POSIXct(forcing$time, tz = "UTC")
head(forcing, 3)
c(rows = nrow(forcing), same_length = nrow(forcing) == nrow(observed),
  step_hours = as.numeric(diff(forcing$time[1:2]), units = "hours"),
  missing_rain = sum(is.na(forcing$rain)), missing_flow = sum(is.na(observed$q_m3s)))
```

Check four things before going further: the two files line up row for row; the time step is
what you think; no rain or evaporation is missing (the model cannot run through a gap in its
inputs, so fill or trim it); and how much flow is missing (gaps in flow are fine: they are
simply left out of the scores).

# 3. Set up a model

Start from the standard PDM and give it your catchment's area and time step:

```{r configure}
config <- pdm_presets("standard")
config$area_km2 <- 64
config$dt <- 1 # time step in hours
str(config, max.level = 1)
```

A configuration is a plain list. Each part is described in
[How the PDM works](pdm-explained.html) and [Choosing model components](model-options.html);
`parameter_catalog()` lists every parameter with its units.

```{r model}
model <- pdm_from_config(config)
```

# 4. Choose a starting state

The model needs to know how wet the catchment is at the start. The simplest good choice is
to start from the first measured flow, assuming the catchment is steady at that moment and
that most of the flow is groundwater:

```{r start}
start <- initial_state_from_flow(model, observed_m3s = observed$q_m3s[1],
                                 baseflow_fraction = 0.7)
```

[Starting a run](starting-states.html) explains the other options and why this matters.

# 5. Run it

```{r run}
result <- run_pdm(model, forcing, start)
simulated <- result$output
names(simulated)
```

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `q_m3s` | Simulated river flow, mean over the time step |
| `soil_mm` | Water in the soil |
| `saturated_fraction` | Share of the catchment where rain runs straight off |
| `aet_mm` | Actual evaporation |
| `surface_out_mm`, `baseflow_out_mm` | The fast and slow parts of the flow |
| `balance_error_mm` | Water-balance check; zero to rounding |

`result$state` holds the stores at the end, ready to carry on from.

# 6. Look at it

```{r plot, fig.cap="Measured (points) and simulated (line) flow with the standard settings."}
plot_flow <- function(sim, label) {
  par(mar = c(3, 4.2, 0.6, 0.6))
  plot(forcing$time, observed$q_m3s, pch = 16, cex = 0.25, col = pal[5], xlab = "",
       ylab = "Flow (m3/s)", ylim = range(c(observed$q_m3s, sim), na.rm = TRUE))
  lines(forcing$time, sim, col = pal[1], lwd = 1.5)
  legend("topleft", c("measured", label), col = c(pal[5], pal[1]), pch = c(16, NA),
         lty = c(NA, 1), lwd = c(NA, 1.5), bty = "n")
}
plot_flow(simulated$q_m3s, "standard settings")
```

# 7. Score it

Leave out the first two weeks, while the model's stores settle, and score the rest:

```{r score}
scored <- (24 * 14 + 1):n
first <- pdm_scorecard(simulated$q_m3s[scored], observed$q_m3s[scored])
round(first[c("nse", "kge", "volume_error", "peak_error", "fdc_high", "fdc_low")], 3)
```

NSE and KGE are 1 for a perfect fit, so `r round(first[["nse"]], 2)` is poor. The total volume
is close (volume error `r sprintf("%+.0f", 100 * first[["volume_error"]])` per cent), so the
amount of water is about right; the problem is how it is shared out over time. The
flow-duration scores `fdc_high` and `fdc_low` say the floods and the low flows are both off,
which points at how quickly water drains to groundwater, and how quickly the surface stores
empty. [Scoring a simulation](scoring.html) explains every score and what it points to.

# 8. Improve it

Let the computer adjust the settings the scores point to: the drainage time constant `kg`,
the two fast stores' time constants, and the rainfall factor `fc` for good measure. The first
half of the record is used to fit, and the second half is kept back to check.

```{r calibrate}
bounds <- calibration_bounds(config)
pick <- c("fc", "recharge.kg", "surface.k1", "surface.k2")
bounds <- bounds[bounds$path %in% pick, ]
fit <- calibrate_pdm(config, forcing[1:(24 * 45), ], observed$q_m3s[1:(24 * 45)],
                     lower = stats::setNames(bounds$lower, bounds$path),
                     upper = stats::setNames(bounds$upper, bounds$path),
                     warmup = 24 * 14, objective = "nse", starts = 3, seed = 1,
                     log_scale = c("recharge.kg", "surface.k1", "surface.k2"),
                     control = list(maxit = 60))
round(fit$parameters, 2)
better <- run_pdm(fit$model, forcing, initial_state_from_flow(fit$model, observed$q_m3s[1], 0.7))
check <- (24 * 45 + 1):n
keep <- c("nse", "kge", "volume_error", "peak_error")
round(rbind(
  standard = pdm_scorecard(simulated$q_m3s[check], observed$q_m3s[check])[keep],
  calibrated = pdm_scorecard(better$output$q_m3s[check], observed$q_m3s[check])[keep]
), 3)
```

```{r plot-better, fig.cap="After calibration, on the whole record. The second half was not used to fit."}
plot_flow(better$output$q_m3s, "calibrated")
abline(v = forcing$time[24 * 45], lty = 2, col = pal[7])
```

The scores in the table are on the second half only, which the calibration never saw: that
is the honest measure of the improvement. [Automatic calibration, explained](auto-calibration.html)
covers the settings used here.

# 9. Save it

Save the configuration as a YAML file you can read, edit and share, and the final state so
the next run can carry on exactly where this one stopped. Use `write_pdm_config()` rather
than a general YAML writer, which would round the calibrated values:

```{r save}
write_pdm_config(fit$config, file.path(folder, "my-catchment.yml"))
saveRDS(better$state, file.path(folder, "end-state.rds"))
again <- load_pdm_model(file.path(folder, "my-catchment.yml"))
identical(pdm_fingerprint(again), pdm_fingerprint(fit$model))
```

The fingerprint check confirms the model read back from the file is exactly the one that was
calibrated.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(folder, recursive = TRUE)
```
